messages:
mandy.supp: Customer (Acme) reports SDK import failing in production after a deploy. They use Poetry and see an ImportError from cryptography which cascades to auth failures and repeated retries from their job: 

mandy.supp: pasted their short log — asked them for env details, pip, python, OS.

acme snippet pasted by customer: 

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/redwood/__init__.py", line 12, in <module>
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes
ImportError: cannot import name 'default_backend' from 'cryptography.hazmat.backends' (/app/.venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/cryptography/hazmat/backends/__init__.py)
```

mandy.supp: They say it started after a CI lockfile update and that Poetry pulled cryptography 40.x. Their jobs then continuously retry auth initialization and eventually fail with 401s on our API because the SDK never finishes init.

tim.sdk: classic dependency surface problem. asking: which python, pip and whether they deploy on Alpine/musl? Also request `poetry.lock` snippet and `pyproject.toml` extras (they might be using `[tool.poetry.extras]`).

mandy.supp: replied with env: Python 3.9.13, pip 20.2.3 (old), Linux (Debian in docker), but CI image is slim so they sometimes hit no-wheel builds. poetry.lock shows cryptography 40.0.0.

oliver.devex: quick note — cryptography changed some public APIs in recent major; our SDK still imports `default_backend` in the auth helper which triggers the ImportError when cryptography removes/renames that symbol. Two paths: (A) instruct customer to pin cryptography to a compatible range or upgrade SDK; (B) if they can't change deps, apply env fixes so cryptography wheels install properly.

oliver.devex: suggested workarounds to customer (short):
```
# recommended first steps
pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel
# if using Poetry explicitly pin
poetry add "cryptography<40"
# or upgrade SDK to the patched release
pip install redwood-sdk==1.5.2
```

oliver.devex: also callout for musl/Alpine builds — if they see `manylinux wheel not found` then they must either install build deps or use an image with manylinux wheels:
```
# Alpine build deps
apk add --no-cache build-base libffi-dev openssl-dev cargo
# Debian/Ubuntu build deps
apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential libssl-dev libffi-dev python3-dev cargo
```

mandy.supp: customer says they can't change base image in the short term and pip is old in their image; we'll try the `pip upgrade` and pin cryptography for now. They asked for a short reproducible command sequence to send to their infra team.

tim.sdk: addendum — we have a patch on main that removes `default_backend` usage and adds a runtime fallback with a clearer error. I'll push a release candidate today. In the meantime pin or upgrade as above. I'll also add a CI test for poetry/resolved-lock scenarios.

lucas.pkg: I've prepared a small release (1.5.2) that is purely import-safe. CI green, changelog includes: "remove legacy cryptography API usage; clearer import-time error message". Will cut release in next hour — tag me if you want me to expedite for the customer.

mandy.supp: thanks — please cut the release and ping me. I'll provide the customer the immediate workaround and ask them to validate the pip upgrade + `poetry add "cryptography<40"` path. Also mention they should re-run `poetry lock --no-update` after pinning.

tim.sdk: one more troubleshooting tip for them: if `pip install` still tries to build cryptography from source, encourage them to use a manylinux base or prebuild wheels in CI cache. Example command to force binary wheel (will fail if wheel not available):
```
pip install --only-binary=:all: cryptography
```

mandy.supp: customer confirmed pip upgrade fixed wheel resolution in their quick test and pin avoided the import error. They will test the SDK 1.5.2 once released and follow up if auth retries persist.

mandy.supp: closing loop — thanks all :thumbsup:
